findings.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial key has no identity type, so "anonymous:0" and "render:0" (both UserUID "0") share an entry: an anonymous visitor denied on a dashboard makes the renderer, which has a hardcoded "*" read grant, get denied on that dashboard for 30s, breaking image rendering and reporting.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — A warm permCache no longer answers denials: every Check not allowed by cached perms runs a full permissionStore.GetUserPermissions query, where before one cached map was reused. A caller or anonymous user probing distinct or random names therefore forces one DB query per name, and singleflight only merges concurrent duplicates.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — The denial cache is checked before the cached perms and is never invalidated. After a grant, a DB refresh from any other denied Check writes the new allow into permCache, but a denial already cached for this resource still wins for up to shortCacheTTL, which defeats the "fallback to the database on outdated cache" behavior this change adds.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:982 — Silent pass: the "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" test seeds permCache with {dash1:false}, and setupService's fakeStore returns no permissions, so Check still denies when the denial-cache lookup at service.go:116-121 is removed. No test proves a DB deny writes to the denial cache either.

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — With NoopCache on the in-proc client, the 30s client-side result cache is gone, so every Check reaches the server. That removes the buffer in front of the new DB-on-every-deny path at service.go:139 and adds a JSON decode of the full scope map on every call, so fan-out Checks can cascade into DB load.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — The denial key joins name and parent with "_", which UIDs may contain, so dashboard "a_b" in folder "c" and dashboard "a" in folder "b_c" share one key. If a user opens a crafted resource they can't access, a false denial is cached on their legitimate resource for 30s (fails closed).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — Denial entries are keyed on caller-supplied Name and ParentFolder with no bound, so Checks on random names flood the shared cache. In-proc, the local cache holds expired 30s entries until its 10-minute cleanup; with a remote cache, they add eviction pressure on perm and folder entries.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — For unknown or unresolvable users, getCachedIdentityPermissions' GetUserIdentifiers error is swallowed and getUserPermissions repeats the same store lookup, so each such Check or List makes two identity DB queries (errors are not cached).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial cache key omits identity type, so "anonymous:0" and "render:0" (both UserUID "0") share denial entries and a cached anonymous denial wrongly denies the renderer (which is granted "*" for dashboards/folders/datasources read) for up to 30s.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with "_", which UIDs can contain, so (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") map to the same key and a denial for one resource falsely denies the other.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions duplicates the identity-type switch, unsupported-type error, and cache-key construction of getIdentityPermissions/getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions, so keying or type handling can silently diverge between cache read and write paths

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — getCachedIdentityPermissions is named as a cache-only lookup but calls GetUserIdentifiers (which queries the store on miss), and Check/List treat every error from it, DB failures included, as a plain cache miss

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey reuses the ".perm_" namespace of userPermCacheKey in the same shared backing cache, even though it holds a different value type (bool vs map), which blurs key ownership and invites collisions

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial key is built from the raw checkReq.UserUID (which may be a numeric ID), while the perm cache key uses the resolved userIdentifiers.UID, so the same user is keyed two different ways across the related caches

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — Check now has two near-identical checkPermission/error-log/requestCount/response blocks (cached path and DB path), plus a third early-return block for the denial cache, where one "resolve perms, then check once" flow would do

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — permissionCacheUsage moved from getUserPermissions into Check/List and now also counts renderer (always a "miss") and cached-but-denied lookups as misses, which quietly changes what the metric means

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:379 — getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions still compute userPermKey/anonPermKey, but after the lookup was removed these keys only drive singleflight and Set, so the "cache key" naming no longer matches what these functions do

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239 — NoopCache is exported from package authz with no doc comment and no interface assertion, only used within the package, and has pointer receivers named `lc` copied from the local cache; it should be unexported (or taken from authlib if there is an equivalent)

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:160 — Removing newRBACClient duplicates the authzlib.NewClient construction at two call sites, and newRemoteRBACClient adds a pointless `client :=` then `return client, nil` step

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:55 — Service struct comment ("Cache for user permissions, user team memberships and user basic roles") was not updated to cover the new permDenialCache field (it already omitted idCache and folderCache)
pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:337 — Removing the only cacheHit=true case leaves the cacheHit field and the `if tc.cacheHit` branches in TestService_getUserPermissions as dead test code

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:981 — Comment says the permCache entry "allows access to prove this is not checked", but it sets dashboards:uid:dash1 to false, which checkPermission treats as a denial, so the test cannot tell whether the denial-cache short-circuit is what caused the deny

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — When permCache is warm but the check is not allowed, Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which no longer consults permCache, so the first deny for every distinct resource triggers a full GetUserPermissions DB query (singleflight only dedups concurrent calls) where it was previously served from cache.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:146 — On the cache-hit-but-denied path checkPermission runs twice, so buildFolderTree fetches and JSON-unmarshals the whole namespace folder tree from cache (a remote round trip in grpc mode) twice per denied Check.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — The denial cache writes one entry per (namespace, user, action, name, folder), so deny-heavy traffic like per-item filtering produces an unbounded keyspace; in-proc these entries sit in the unbounded local cache until the 10-minute janitor runs, and in remote mode they add eviction pressure on the permission and folder entries.

pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — Switching the in-proc authz client to NoopCache drops the 30s client-side Check/List result cache, so every call now goes through the server path and JSON-unmarshals the full scope map (and folder tree) instead of returning a cached bool or list.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — The permDenialCache lookup happens on every Check, including ones that end up allowed, which adds an extra cache round trip per request when the service is backed by the shared remote cache.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — GetUserIdentifiers runs in both getCachedIdentityPermissions and getUserPermissions, and errors from the first call are swallowed, so an idCache miss or an unknown user repeats the identifier DB query within the same request.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — Any deny from cached perms now falls through to getIdentityPermissions, and getUserPermissions no longer reads permCache, so every distinct denied resource triggers a permission-store DB query (previously served from the 30s perm cache); together with the in-proc client switching to NoopCache (rbac.go:103), per-item Check fan-out (e.g. filtering N search results) becomes N DB queries.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — Errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions (e.g. a GetUserIdentifiers DB failure) are dropped without logging and getIdentityPermissions calls GetUserIdentifiers again, so every failing request hits the DB twice; when the cache backend is down (cacheWrap.Set fails silently), every user Check/List does two identity DB lookups plus extra cache round-trips (same pattern in List at line 180).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with "_", and Grafana UIDs can contain "_", so (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") share one key; a denial cached for one resource then wrongly denies the other for up to 30s.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:354 — The render service always returns ErrNotFound from getCachedIdentityPermissions, and anonymous/render requests are now counted too, so every renderer Check/List increments permissionCacheUsage "false" and skews the cache hit-rate metric.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — Every denied Check writes a denial-cache entry keyed on caller-supplied Name/ParentFolder, so the number of cache entries is unbounded (before, it was capped at one per user+action); the in-proc local cache only evicts every 10 min, so floods of checks on distinct names can exhaust memory

pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — The denial cache key joins name and parent with an ambiguous "_" (e.g. name "x_y" + folder "z" vs name "x" + folder "y_z", and Grafana UIDs allow "_"), so a denial cached for one resource falsely denies a different resource (fails closed, availability only)

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial key uses the raw subject UID with no identity type, and anonymous/render subject IDs are never resolved, so a caller sending "anonymous:<victimUID>" can store denials that block a real user with that UID for 30s

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:982 — "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" seeds permCache with {dash1: false} (contradicting its "Allow access" comment) and the default fakeStore returns no permissions, so Check still denies if the denial-cache short-circuit at service.go:116-121 is removed, which means the test passes without proving anything.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — No test checks that a deny on the DB path writes to permDenialCache: the existing "should deny user without permission" case only checks permCache, so the write side of the new denial cache has no coverage.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — No test covers a stale denial-cache entry blocking a newly granted permission for up to shortCacheTTL; permCache gets this coverage through the "outdated cache" fallback test, but the denial cache does not.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:337 — The cacheHit field in TestService_getUserPermissions is now false in every case, so the branches at lines 367 and 388 are dead and wrongly suggest getIdentityPermissions still reads the cache.

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — No test covers getCachedIdentityPermissions' error paths (a GetUserIdentifiers failure or an unsupported type is silently treated as a cache miss in Check and List) or its anonymous permCache-hit branch at line 349.
pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — The in-process RBAC client was switched to the new NoopCache type, which removes client-side caching, and no test was added or updated for this.

goldens.comment: The Check operation exhibits asymmetric cache trust logic: cached permission grants are trusted and returned immediately, but cached denials from the same permission cache are ignored, leading to a fresh database lookup. This allows stale cached grants to provide access to revoked resources, posing a security risk.
The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.

The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial key has no identity type, so "anonymous:0" and "render:0" (both UserUID "0") share an entry: an anonymous visitor denied on a dashboard makes the renderer, which has a hardcoded "*" read grant, get denied on that dashboard for 30s, breaking image rendering and reporting.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `permDenialCache` lookup keyed by `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` (service.go: `permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, ...)`). The key does not include `checkReq.IdentityType`, so different identity types that share the same `UserUID` within a namespace would share denial entries and could incorrectly deny each other. However, the specific claim that anonymous and render identities both have `UserUID == "0"` and that render has a hardcoded "*" grant is not verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — A warm permCache no longer answers denials: every Check not allowed by cached perms runs a full permissionStore.GetUserPermissions query, where before one cached map was reused. A caller or anonymous user probing distinct or random names therefore forces one DB query per name, and singleflight only merges concurrent duplicates.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the new cache-fast-path returns early only when cached perms allow (`if allowed { ... return }`). If cached perms exist but do *not* allow, it falls through to `s.getIdentityPermissions(...)`, which will hit the store/DB. Previously, `getUserPermissions` (and anonymous) checked `s.permCache` and could return a cached permissions map that would then be used to deny without querying. The diff also removes those cache checks in `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions` and adds `permDenialCache`, but that denial cache is keyed by `(namespace,user,action,name,parent)` so probing distinct names will still bypass it and trigger a DB fetch per name. This is a performance/DoS-surface regression rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — The denial cache is checked before the cached perms and is never invalidated. After a grant, a DB refresh from any other denied Check writes the new allow into permCache, but a denial already cached for this resource still wins for up to shortCacheTTL, which defeats the "fallback to the database on outdated cache" behavior this change adds.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the code checks permDenialCache first and returns Allowed:false immediately if the key exists (new block around service.go:113+). Later, when a DB lookup determines the request is allowed, the code does not delete/clear any existing denial entry for the same permDenialKey; it only sets permDenialCache when !allowed (service.go:150+). Therefore a previously cached denial will continue to override both cached allows and any fresh DB allow until the denial cache entry expires (shortCacheTTL). This defeats the intended “fallback to the database on outdated cache” behavior for the specific resource once a grant happens.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:982 — Silent pass: the "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" test seeds permCache with {dash1:false}, and setupService's fakeStore returns no permissions, so Check still denies when the denial-cache lookup at service.go:116-121 is removed. No test proves a DB deny writes to the denial cache either.

adjudication.rationale: The new denial-cache short-circuit is implemented in Service.Check (service.go:113-121), but the added test "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" is not actually proving that logic is used. In that test, permCache is seeded with map{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false} (service_test.go in the new TestService_CacheCheck), and there is no store permission setup that would allow the request; so even if the permDenialCache lookup were removed, Check would still end up denying (cached check returns not-allowed and falls through to DB, which also denies). Also, no test asserts that a DB-derived deny triggers the new write `s.permDenialCache.Set(..., true)` (service.go:150-152).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — With NoopCache on the in-proc client, the 30s client-side result cache is gone, so every Check reaches the server. That removes the buffer in front of the new DB-on-every-deny path at service.go:139 and adds a JSON decode of the full scope map on every call, so fan-out Checks can cascade into DB load.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly replaces the in-proc RBAC client construction with `authzlib.NewClient(..., authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...)` in `ProvideAuthZClient` (rbac.go), and the added `NoopCache` always returns `cache.ErrNotFound` on `Get`, so the authzlib client-side cache is effectively disabled for in-proc calls. Separately, `Service.Check` now tries cached perms and, if they don’t allow, falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` (DB-backed) and only then sets a per-resource deny cache (`permDenialCache`), so increased request volume to the server can translate into more DB work. The finding’s performance concern is diff-grounded, though the specific “JSON decode of the full scope map” detail isn’t verifiable from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — The denial key joins name and parent with "_", which UIDs may contain, so dashboard "a_b" in folder "c" and dashboard "a" in folder "b_c" share one key. If a user opens a crafted resource they can't access, a false denial is cached on their legitimate resource for 30s (fails closed).

pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — Denial entries are keyed on caller-supplied Name and ParentFolder with no bound, so Checks on random names flood the shared cache. In-proc, the local cache holds expired 30s entries until its 10-minute cleanup; with a remote cache, they add eviction pressure on perm and folder entries.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new negative-result cache `permDenialCache` in `Service.Check` keyed by `userPermDenialCacheKey(ns, userUID, action, name, parent)` (service.go: new cache + lookup/set; cache.go: key builder). Because `name` and `parent` come from the request (`CheckRequest`), a caller can generate many unique keys by varying these fields, causing unbounded cache key growth/eviction pressure until TTL expiry. This is a security/perf defect introduced by the change. However, the finding’s specific claim about “in-proc local cache holds expired 30s entries until its 10-minute cleanup” is not fully supported for this denial cache by the diff (that 30s/10m config appears in the *remote client* cache, and in-proc client caching is disabled via `NoopCache`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — For unknown or unresolvable users, getCachedIdentityPermissions' GetUserIdentifiers error is swallowed and getUserPermissions repeats the same store lookup, so each such Check or List makes two identity DB queries (errors are not cached).

adjudication.rationale: In both `Service.Check` and `Service.List`, the new flow calls `getCachedIdentityPermissions(...)` first. For `TypeUser`/`TypeServiceAccount`, that function calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` and returns an error if it fails (service.go `getCachedIdentityPermissions`). However, `Check` only uses the cached result when `err == nil`; any non-nil error (including identity lookup failures) is treated like a cache miss and it proceeds to call `s.getIdentityPermissions(...)`, which (via `getUserPermissions`) will call `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` again. The same pattern exists in `List` where it falls back on any `err != nil`. This can cause two identity-store lookups per request on unresolvable/errored users, but the final behavior is still to error out, so it’s primarily a performance/edge-case handling concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial cache key omits identity type, so "anonymous:0" and "render:0" (both UserUID "0") share denial entries and a cached anonymous denial wrongly denies the renderer (which is granted "*" for dashboards/folders/datasources read) for up to 30s.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the denial cache key is built as userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, checkReq.UserUID, action, name, parentFolder) and consulted before any identity-type-specific logic. The key function (added in cache.go) also omits identity type. Since Check handles different identity types (see getCachedIdentityPermissions switch on idType) but the denial cache does not, two different identities that share the same UserUID string would collide and a cached denial for one identity type could incorrectly deny the other for the TTL window.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with "_", which UIDs can contain, so (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") map to the same key and a denial for one resource falsely denies the other.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace, userUID, action, name, parent)` which builds a cache key via simple string concatenation with "_" separators: `... + "_" + name + "_" + parent` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go). This construction is inherently ambiguous if `name` or `parent` can contain "_", because different (name,parent) pairs could produce the same key and cause an unrelated denial to be reused in `Service.Check` via `permDenialCache.Get(...)` (pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go). However, the diff does not establish that these fields can contain underscores, so the claim that this will happen for UIDs is not strictly verifiable from the PR alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:342 — getCachedIdentityPermissions duplicates the identity-type switch, unsupported-type error, and cache-key construction of getIdentityPermissions/getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions, so keying or type handling can silently diverge between cache read and write paths

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `getCachedIdentityPermissions` with its own identity-type `switch`, `unsupported identity type` error, and cache-key construction (`anonymousPermCacheKey`, `GetUserIdentifiers` + `userPermCacheKey`). Cache writes still occur in the separate paths (`getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions`) using similar key construction. While the current keys/type handling appear consistent, the duplication creates a real maintenance risk that the cache-read and cache-write logic can diverge silently in future edits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — getCachedIdentityPermissions is named as a cache-only lookup but calls GetUserIdentifiers (which queries the store on miss), and Check/List treat every error from it, DB failures included, as a plain cache miss

adjudication.rationale: In `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (added at `service.go` around the new function), the user/service-account path calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(ctx, ns, userID)` before attempting the permissions cache lookup. That makes the function not purely “cache-only” in terms of dependencies, and it can trigger extra work (and potentially a store lookup) just to decide whether permissions are cached. Additionally, both `Check` and `List` treat any non-nil error from `getCachedIdentityPermissions` as a cache miss and fall back to `getIdentityPermissions` (`if err == nil { ... } else { ... }`), which means unexpected errors from the identifier step are not distinguished at the cache-lookup layer and may lead to redundant retries and misleading cache-miss metrics, even if the ultimate DB error may still surface later.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:30 — userPermDenialCacheKey reuses the ".perm_" namespace of userPermCacheKey in the same shared backing cache, even though it holds a different value type (bool vs map), which blurs key ownership and invites collisions

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses the same `.perm_` prefix as `userPermCacheKey` while storing a different value type (`bool` vs `map[string]bool`) in the same backing cache. However, the new key appends `"_"+name+"_"+parent`, so it does not inherently collide with the existing `userPermCacheKey` form unless the concatenated components can produce identical full strings (e.g., if fields contain underscores / ambiguous concatenations). The finding is therefore a real robustness/maintainability concern grounded in the diff, but not a definitively proven runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — Denial key is built from the raw checkReq.UserUID (which may be a numeric ID), while the perm cache key uses the resolved userIdentifiers.UID, so the same user is keyed two different ways across the related caches

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the new denial cache key is built with `checkReq.UserUID` (`userPermDenialCacheKey(checkReq.Namespace.Value, checkReq.UserUID, ...)`), while the permission cache path for user/service-account identities resolves identifiers via `GetUserIdentifiers(...)` and keys permissions with `userIdentifiers.UID` (`userPermCacheKey(ns.Value, userIdentifiers.UID, action)`). This is a real inconsistency in how the same user is keyed across related caches, which can reduce cache effectiveness if requests can represent the same user via different `UserUID` strings. However, it does not appear to cause incorrect allow/deny outcomes because on a cache miss the code falls back to DB evaluation; it primarily affects caching behavior/performance.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — Check now has two near-identical checkPermission/error-log/requestCount/response blocks (cached path and DB path), plus a third early-return block for the denial cache, where one "resolve perms, then check once" flow would do

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, the diff adds (1) an early-return denial-cache block and (2) a cached-permissions path that calls `s.checkPermission(...)`, logs on error, increments `requestCount`, and returns a `CheckResponse` on allow. The function then falls through to the existing DB path, which again fetches permissions and calls `s.checkPermission(...)` with similar error logging/metrics/response handling. This is verifiable duplication introduced by the change (maintainability/readability), not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:137 — permissionCacheUsage moved from getUserPermissions into Check/List and now also counts renderer (always a "miss") and cached-but-denied lookups as misses, which quietly changes what the metric means

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes permissionCacheUsage increments from getUserPermissions (and implicit cache checks there) and adds metric increments in Check/List based on getCachedIdentityPermissions. In Check, when cached permissions exist but do not allow the specific request, it falls through and increments permissionCacheUsage with "false" (miss) even though the cache was consulted (cachedPerms was present but allowed==false). Also, getCachedIdentityPermissions explicitly returns cache.ErrNotFound for types.TypeRenderService, so renderer requests will always be counted as "false" (miss). This is a real, diff-grounded change in metric semantics/interpretation, but it does not clearly introduce a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:379 — getUserPermissions/getAnonymousPermissions still compute userPermKey/anonPermKey, but after the lookup was removed these keys only drive singleflight and Set, so the "cache key" naming no longer matches what these functions do

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions` still compute `userPermKey`/`anonPermKey` and use them to key `singleflight` (`s.sf.Do(userPermKey+"_getUserPermissions", ...)`, `s.sf.Do(anonPermKey+"_getAnonymousPermissions", ...)`). Also, the caching behavior was moved to `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (new function) for the read path; the keys still represent cache keys for permission entries even if the `Get` lookup was removed from these functions. The claim that the naming “no longer matches what these functions do” is not supported by the diff as shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:239 — NoopCache is exported from package authz with no doc comment and no interface assertion, only used within the package, and has pointer receivers named `lc` copied from the local cache; it should be unexported (or taken from authlib if there is an equivalent)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add an exported `type NoopCache struct{}` in `pkg/services/authz/rbac.go` without a doc comment, and it is used as `authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{})`. However, the finding’s claims that it is “only used within the package” and that it needs an “interface assertion” are not verifiable from this diff, and the doc-comment/exported-name complaint is primarily a style/lint nit rather than a concrete defect or substantial review issue grounded in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:160 — Removing newRBACClient duplicates the authzlib.NewClient construction at two call sites, and newRemoteRBACClient adds a pointless `client :=` then `return client, nil` step

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `authzlib.NewClient(...)` being constructed in two places (in `ProvideAuthZClient` and inside `newRemoteRBACClient`) and `newRemoteRBACClient` now uses a temporary `client := ...; return client, nil` that could be inlined. However, this is a stylistic/refactoring nit rather than a verifiable defect or substantive review issue. Also, the two constructions are intentionally different (local path uses `NoopCache`, remote path uses `cache.NewLocalCache(...)`), so it's not clearly an avoidable duplication caused by removing `newRBACClient`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:55 — Service struct comment ("Cache for user permissions, user team memberships and user basic roles") was not updated to cover the new permDenialCache field (it already omitted idCache and folderCache)

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add a new field `permDenialCache` to `Service` (service.go) without updating the nearby struct comment, but this is only a documentation/comment nit (and the comment was already incomplete, omitting `idCache` and `folderCache`). It does not represent a functional defect or a substantive review issue grounded in behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:337 — Removing the only cacheHit=true case leaves the cacheHit field and the `if tc.cacheHit` branches in TestService_getUserPermissions as dead test code

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes the only shown test case in `TestService_getUserPermissions` that explicitly sets `cacheHit: true` (lines around the removed block in `service_test.go`). If no other cases set `cacheHit: true`, then any `cacheHit` field in the testCase struct and any `if tc.cacheHit` logic in the test would become dead/unexercised test code. This is a test-maintenance issue, not a production defect, but the diff snippet alone doesn’t show the struct/branches to fully confirm.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:981 — Comment says the permCache entry "allows access to prove this is not checked", but it sets dashboards:uid:dash1 to false, which checkPermission treats as a denial, so the test cannot tell whether the denial-cache short-circuit is what caused the deny
matched_golden_ids: The test comment says the cached permissions 'allow access', but the map stores false for dashboards:uid:dash1, so checkPermission will still treat this scope as not allowed.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both point out the same inconsistency: the test comment claims the cached permissions entry "allows access," but the cache map sets dashboards:uid:dash1 to false, which checkPermission interprets as a denial. The candidate also explains the consequence (test can’t prove the intended behavior), aligning with the golden issue.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — When permCache is warm but the check is not allowed, Check falls through to getIdentityPermissions, which no longer consults permCache, so the first deny for every distinct resource triggers a full GetUserPermissions DB query (singleflight only dedups concurrent calls) where it was previously served from cache.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes cache a fast-path only for ALLOW in `Service.Check`: it calls `getCachedIdentityPermissions` and returns early only if `allowed` is true; if cached perms do not allow, it falls through to `getIdentityPermissions` (which calls `getUserPermissions`/`getAnonymousPermissions`). In this PR, the direct `permCache.Get(...)` checks inside `getUserPermissions` and `getAnonymousPermissions` were removed, so `getIdentityPermissions` will no longer use `permCache` to avoid the store call. As a result, the first deny for a (user, action, resource) will indeed hit the DB even if `permCache` is warm, until `permDenialCache` is populated (which only happens after a DB-backed deny). This is a performance/behavior tradeoff rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:146 — On the cache-hit-but-denied path checkPermission runs twice, so buildFolderTree fetches and JSON-unmarshals the whole namespace folder tree from cache (a remote round trip in grpc mode) twice per denied Check.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check`, when `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns cached perms and `s.checkPermission` returns `allowed == false`, the code falls through and later calls `s.checkPermission` again after fetching fresh permissions via `getIdentityPermissions` (see the new early-cache block around the added `cachedPerms` logic, then the existing DB path below). That means the permission evaluation work can run twice on the cache-hit-but-denied path. The finding’s specific claim about `buildFolderTree` and “remote round trip in grpc mode” isn’t directly verifiable from this diff (those implementations aren’t shown), but the double `checkPermission` call itself is real and can cause redundant work.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — The denial cache writes one entry per (namespace, user, action, name, folder), so deny-heavy traffic like per-item filtering produces an unbounded keyspace; in-proc these entries sit in the unbounded local cache until the 10-minute janitor runs, and in remote mode they add eviction pressure on the permission and folder entries.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new permDenialCache in Service (service.go) and a cache key function userPermDenialCacheKey(namespace,userUID,action,name,parent) (cache.go). In Check(), on any denied result it does `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` and on subsequent requests it returns early if that exact key is present. This is indeed one cache entry per (namespace, user, action, name, parent-folder), which can grow very large under deny-heavy / per-item checks and shares the same underlying cache instance as other caches (permCache, folderCache, etc.), so it can increase memory/eviction pressure. However, the claim about entries sitting until a "10-minute janitor" is not directly verifiable for this denial cache from the diff (the 10-minute cleanup interval shown is for the *client* local cache in newRemoteRBACClient, not necessarily the Service cache), so the concern is valid but some specifics are overstated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — Switching the in-proc authz client to NoopCache drops the 30s client-side Check/List result cache, so every call now goes through the server path and JSON-unmarshals the full scope map (and folder tree) instead of returning a cached bool or list.

adjudication.rationale: In `ProvideAuthZClient`, the in-proc client is changed from `newRBACClient(channel, tracer)` (which, per the removed helper, configured a `cache.NewLocalCache` with 30s expiry) to `authzlib.NewClient(..., authzlib.WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...)`, which disables client-side caching for the in-proc path. The remote client path (`newRemoteRBACClient`) still uses the 30s local cache. This is a concrete performance/architecture regression risk (more calls traversing the gRPC server/service path) but not a correctness defect. The specific claim about JSON-unmarshalling full maps/trees is not verifiable from this diff alone (client internals aren’t shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — The permDenialCache lookup happens on every Check, including ones that end up allowed, which adds an extra cache round trip per request when the service is backed by the shared remote cache.

adjudication.rationale: In `Service.Check` the new logic unconditionally computes `permDenialKey` and calls `s.permDenialCache.Get(...)` before any other caching/permission evaluation (added around the start of `Check`). This means every `Check` request incurs an extra cache lookup even when the request is ultimately allowed (e.g., when `getCachedIdentityPermissions` hits and `allowed` is true). The diff doesn’t show this causing incorrect authorization decisions, but it is a concrete performance/architecture concern if `permDenialCache` is backed by a shared/remote cache.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — GetUserIdentifiers runs in both getCachedIdentityPermissions and getUserPermissions, and errors from the first call are swallowed, so an idCache miss or an unknown user repeats the identifier DB query within the same request.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `getCachedIdentityPermissions` calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` for `TypeUser`/`TypeServiceAccount` (new function in `service.go`), and `getUserPermissions` also calls `s.GetUserIdentifiers(...)` before computing permissions. In `Check` (and similarly `List`), the result of `getCachedIdentityPermissions` is only used when `err == nil`; any error (including non-`cache.ErrNotFound` errors from `GetUserIdentifiers`) is ignored and the code falls back to `getIdentityPermissions`, which can trigger a second `GetUserIdentifiers` call in the same request path. This is a real, diff-grounded inefficiency/duplicate-query concern, but it doesn’t clearly introduce incorrect behavior by itself (it likely just repeats work and may retry on real errors).

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:139 — Any deny from cached perms now falls through to getIdentityPermissions, and getUserPermissions no longer reads permCache, so every distinct denied resource triggers a permission-store DB query (previously served from the 30s perm cache); together with the in-proc client switching to NoopCache (rbac.go:103), per-item Check fan-out (e.g. filtering N search results) becomes N DB queries.

adjudication.rationale: Diff shows a performance/behavior change: in Service.Check, cached permissions are only used to early-return on allow; a cached miss/deny falls through to s.getIdentityPermissions (service.go:113-150). Also, getUserPermissions and getAnonymousPermissions no longer consult permCache (service.go:377-421, 421-440), so once Check falls through it will hit the permission store even if the perms map was already cached. The new permDenialCache mitigates repeated denials for the same (action,name,parent) (service.go:111-131, 150-154), but distinct denied resources can still cause additional DB queries. Separately, ProvideAuthZClient now constructs an authzlib client with a NoopCache (rbac.go:98-108), disabling client-side caching in the in-proc case. This is a diff-grounded scalability concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:123 — Errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions (e.g. a GetUserIdentifiers DB failure) are dropped without logging and getIdentityPermissions calls GetUserIdentifiers again, so every failing request hits the DB twice; when the cache backend is down (cacheWrap.Set fails silently), every user Check/List does two identity DB lookups plus extra cache round-trips (same pattern in List at line 180).

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces getCachedIdentityPermissions(), which for user/service-account identities calls s.GetUserIdentifiers() before checking permCache (service.go:339+). In Check() and List(), when getCachedIdentityPermissions returns a non-nil error (including cache.ErrNotFound due to a permCache miss), the code falls back to s.getIdentityPermissions(...) (Check at ~113–150, List at ~177–195). getIdentityPermissions ultimately re-enters the normal permission path that calls GetUserIdentifiers again (e.g., getUserPermissions builds userPermKey from userIdentifiers, service.go:377+). This means on a permission-cache miss with an idCache miss (or if GetUserIdentifiers fails), the request can perform the identity lookup twice and the initial error from getCachedIdentityPermissions is not logged at the call site. This is a performance/observability concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — userPermDenialCacheKey joins name and parent with "_", and Grafana UIDs can contain "_", so (name="a_b", parent="c") and (name="a", parent="b_c") share one key; a denial cached for one resource then wrongly denies the other for up to 30s.
matched_golden_ids: The cache key construction in `userPermDenialCacheKey` uses simple string concatenation with underscores, which can lead to ambiguous keys and collision risks when any component contains underscores or is empty. This could result in incorrect denial cache hits, affecting user permissions.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both comments identify that building the cache key by concatenating components with "_" can create ambiguous keys when components contain underscores (or are otherwise not safely delimited), leading to collisions and incorrect permission denial cache hits.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:354 — The render service always returns ErrNotFound from getCachedIdentityPermissions, and anonymous/render requests are now counted too, so every renderer Check/List increments permissionCacheUsage "false" and skews the cache hit-rate metric.

adjudication.rationale: In `getCachedIdentityPermissions` the `types.TypeRenderService` case unconditionally returns `cache.ErrNotFound` (service.go, added function). Both `Check` and `List` now increment `permissionCacheUsage` with label `"false"` when `getCachedIdentityPermissions` returns an error (Check: after the cache attempt; List: in the `else` branch). Therefore, render-service requests will always be recorded as cache misses even though caching is intentionally not used for that identity type, which can skew the cache hit-rate metric. This is metric/observability correctness rather than functional behavior breakage.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:154 — Every denied Check writes a denial-cache entry keyed on caller-supplied Name/ParentFolder, so the number of cache entries is unbounded (before, it was capped at one per user+action); the in-proc local cache only evicts every 10 min, so floods of checks on distinct names can exhaust memory

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new permDenialCache and in Service.Check unconditionally writes an entry on any denied decision: `permDenialKey := userPermDenialCacheKey(..., checkReq.Name, checkReq.ParentFolder)` and `s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true)` when `!allowed`. Because `Name` and `ParentFolder` come from the request and are part of the key, a caller can generate arbitrarily many distinct keys (unbounded cardinality) vs the prior model that cached only per user+action. With an in-memory cache backend (e.g., local cache in tests/elsewhere), this can grow memory without a hard bound and is an availability/DoS risk introduced by the change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/cache.go:31 — The denial cache key joins name and parent with an ambiguous "_" (e.g. name "x_y" + folder "z" vs name "x" + folder "y_z", and Grafana UIDs allow "_"), so a denial cached for one resource falsely denies a different resource (fails closed, availability only)

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `userPermDenialCacheKey()` which builds a cache key by concatenating `namespace`, `userUID`, `action`, `name`, and `parent` with `_` separators (`namespace + ".perm_" + userUID + "_" + action + "_" + name + "_" + parent`). In `Service.Check`, this key is used to short-circuit and deny (`permDenialCache.Get(...)` -> return `Allowed: false`). Because there is no escaping/length-prefixing, different `(name,parent)` pairs can produce the same key when either component contains `_` (or other boundary ambiguities), causing an unrelated resource to be denied based on a cached denial for another resource. This is a real behavioral defect introduced by the new denial-cache mechanism.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:116 — The denial key uses the raw subject UID with no identity type, and anonymous/render subject IDs are never resolved, so a caller sending "anonymous:<victimUID>" can store denials that block a real user with that UID for 30s

adjudication.rationale: The new denial-cache lookup in `Service.Check` builds `permDenialKey` from `checkReq.Namespace.Value`, `checkReq.UserUID`, `checkReq.Action`, `checkReq.Name`, `checkReq.ParentFolder` and short-circuits to deny if present (service.go). This key does not include `checkReq.IdentityType` and it is computed before any identity-specific normalization/lookup (contrast with `getCachedIdentityPermissions`, which resolves user/service-account identifiers via `GetUserIdentifiers` for `TypeUser`/`TypeServiceAccount` and treats `TypeAnonymous` differently). So denials may collide across identity types or differing UID representations, potentially causing incorrect denials. However, the specific claim that a caller can send `anonymous:<victimUID>` and have it resolve to the victim’s UID is not verifiable from this diff because the subject→`checkReq` parsing logic is not shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:982 — "Should deny on explicit cache deny entry" seeds permCache with {dash1: false} (contradicting its "Allow access" comment) and the default fakeStore returns no permissions, so Check still denies if the denial-cache short-circuit at service.go:116-121 is removed, which means the test passes without proving anything.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly points out a weakness in the new test rather than a functional defect. In `TestService_CacheCheck` ("Should deny on explicit cache deny entry"), the comment says it seeds `permCache` to “Allow access … to prove this is not checked”, but it actually stores `map[string]bool{"dashboards:uid:dash1": false}`. Given the updated `Service.Check` logic, even if the denial-cache short-circuit at `service.go:116-121` were removed, the test would still likely deny: cached permissions would indicate not allowed (false), then the code falls back to `getIdentityPermissions`, and the default `setupService()` uses a fake store that (in this subtest) is not populated with any allow permission. So the test doesn’t uniquely validate the denial-cache short-circuit behavior; it can pass for other reasons.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:153 — No test checks that a deny on the DB path writes to permDenialCache: the existing "should deny user without permission" case only checks permCache, so the write side of the new denial cache has no coverage.

adjudication.rationale: In Service.Check, the DB/fallback path writes to the new denial cache (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(ctx, permDenialKey, true) }`), but the added tests only cover (a) allow via cached perms, (b) fallback to DB for allows, and (c) denial via a pre-populated `permDenialCache` entry. No test asserts that a DB-derived deny actually populates `permDenialCache`, so the write-side behavior of the new denial cache is untested as claimed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:117 — No test covers a stale denial-cache entry blocking a newly granted permission for up to shortCacheTTL; permCache gets this coverage through the "outdated cache" fallback test, but the denial cache does not.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `permDenialCache` checked first in `Service.Check` (service.go: around the added block computing `permDenialKey` and immediately returning `Allowed: false` if present), and it is populated on any computed denial (`if !allowed { s.permDenialCache.Set(...) }`). The added tests cover (1) allow via cached permissions, (2) DB fallback on cache miss, (3) DB fallback on outdated *permCache*, and (4) explicit deny entry causes deny. There is no test exercising the scenario where `permDenialCache` contains a stale deny while the DB (or updated permissions) would allow, which would be blocked until `shortCacheTTL` expires because the function returns before consulting permCache/DB. This is a specific, diff-grounded missing-test gap for newly added logic, not a provable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service_test.go:337 — The cacheHit field in TestService_getUserPermissions is now false in every case, so the branches at lines 367 and 388 are dead and wrongly suggest getIdentityPermissions still reads the cache.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does remove the cache-hit test case from `TestService_getUserPermissions`, but it does not show the remaining test cases or the referenced branches at lines 367/388, so the claim that `cacheHit` is now false in *every* case and that specific branches are dead is not verifiable from the provided diff. Also, the production code now reads cache via the newly added `getCachedIdentityPermissions` (used by `Check`/`List`), so the statement that the tests wrongly suggest `getIdentityPermissions` still reads cache appears to mischaracterize the new cache-reading path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac/service.go:356 — No test covers getCachedIdentityPermissions' error paths (a GetUserIdentifiers failure or an unsupported type is silently treated as a cache miss in Check and List) or its anonymous permCache-hit branch at line 349.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds getCachedIdentityPermissions (service.go) with multiple branches: anonymous cache-hit, user/service-account path that can return a GetUserIdentifiers error, and a default unsupported-type error. The new tests (TestService_CacheCheck/TestService_CacheList) only cover user cache-hit/miss/outdated and denial-cache behavior; they do not exercise the anonymous cache-hit branch, nor any error return from getCachedIdentityPermissions. Also, in Check and List the call pattern is `if err == nil { ... }` else fall back to getIdentityPermissions, so errors from getCachedIdentityPermissions are not handled distinctly from a cache miss; there is no test asserting the intended behavior for those error cases.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/services/authz/rbac.go:103 — The in-process RBAC client was switched to the new NoopCache type, which removes client-side caching, and no test was added or updated for this.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does switch the in-process RBAC client in ProvideAuthZClient from newRBACClient(channel, tracer) to authzlib.NewClient(..., WithCacheClientOption(&NoopCache{}), ...), which effectively disables client-side caching for the in-process path. That’s a concrete behavioral/performance change. However, the finding’s claim that “no test was added or updated” is not strictly true: new tests were added (e.g., TestService_CacheCheck, TestService_CacheList), but they exercise server-side/service caching behavior, not the in-process client’s NoopCache behavior.
